summary: Multi-intent guest questions (e.g. "WiFi password AND breakfast time") return generic summary answers, while the single-intent versions return perfect, specific facts. The cause is a single embedding being averaged across two unrelated topics. Fix: decompose the user message into sub-queries inside handle_knowledge, retrieve top-3 per sub-query, and concatenate as labelled [Q1]/[Q2] blocks (Option A); harden with a "MULTI-INTENT RULE" addendum to the system prompt (Option B) as additive defense.
root_cause: In src/hotel_guardrails/hotel_langgraph.py::handle_knowledge (line ~608) the full user message is passed verbatim to search_hotel_knowledge.invoke(last_user_message). That tool (src/agent/hotel_tools.py line ~847) embeds the entire string once and retrieves num_docs=5 nearest chunks (HOTEL_RAG_NUM_DOCS=5). When the message bundles two distinct intents ("WiFi password AND breakfast hours"), the resulting embedding lies between the two topic clusters in vector space, so the nearest neighbours are generic facility-overview chunks (data/hotel/facilities.md, welcome.md) rather than wifi.md and dining.md. The LLM then faithfully summarises those generic chunks and produces the high-level "we provide breakfast and free WiFi" answer. The chunks containing the actual WiFi password and the 6:30-10:30 breakfast time are never put into the context window.
fix_strategy:
Option A (primary): Add a tiny pure-Python splitter `_split_multi_intent(text)` next to `_maybe_compute_pricing_context` in hotel_langgraph.py that splits on '?', ' and ', ' and also ', ' also ', ' plus ', ';' (EN), ' และ ', ' กับ ' (TH), ' 和 ', ' 还有 ', '、' (CN). Returns ≤4 sub-queries (cap to bound latency). In `handle_knowledge`, when the splitter returns >1 sub-query, run search_hotel_knowledge per sub-query with HOTEL_RAG_NUM_DOCS_PER_SUBQ=3, prefix each block with `[Q{i}: <sub-question>]`, and concatenate with `

===

`. Total context still trimmed to 2000 chars. Single-intent path is unchanged (zero regression risk for single questions). Option B (additive): append a MULTI-INTENT RULE line to the existing `(system, "Use this hotel information…")` block instructing the LLM to answer each [Q#] separately with verbatim facts and forbid high-level summarisation. Both changes are local to handle_knowledge — no schema, no graph topology, no prompt YAML edits required, so the eval pipeline and other sub-agents are untouched.

# --- INSERT after _maybe_compute_pricing_context (~line 578) ---

# Delimiters that signal the guest packed multiple distinct questions into
# one message. We split on these BEFORE embedding so each intent gets its
# own nearest-neighbour search in vector space — a single embedding of a
# multi-intent query lands between topic clusters and retrieves generic
# facility chunks instead of the specific facts (see Defect 2).
_MULTI_INTENT_SPLIT_RE = _re.compile(
    r"\s*(?:\?+|;|\band also\b|\band\b|\balso\b|\bplus\b|"
    r"และ|กับ|"  # th: และ, กับ
    r"和|还有|、)\s*",          # cn: 和, 还有, 、
    _re.IGNORECASE,
)

_INFO_KEYWORDS = (
    "wifi", "password", "breakfast", "pool", "spa", "gym", "check",
    "checkout", "check-in", "check-out", "parking", "laundry", "shuttle",
    "restaurant", "bar", "hour", "time", "where", "when", "how", "what",
    "อาหาร", "สระ", "อินเตอร์เน็ต",  # th: อาหาร, สระ, อินเตอร์เน็ต
    "早餐", "游泳池", "密码",  # cn: 早餐, 游泳池, 密码
)


def _split_multi_intent(text: str, max_parts: int = 4) -> List[str]:
    """Split a guest message into distinct sub-questions for RAG.

    Returns a list of length 1 (no split needed) up to ``max_parts``.
    Conservative: only splits when at least two of the resulting parts
    contain an information keyword, so we don't over-fragment a normal
    single-intent sentence that happens to contain 'and'.
    """
    if not text or len(text) < 12:
        return [text] if text else []
    raw_parts = [p.strip() for p in _MULTI_INTENT_SPLIT_RE.split(text) if p and p.strip()]
    if len(raw_parts) < 2:
        return [text]
    low_text = text.lower()
    informative = [
        p for p in raw_parts
        if any(kw in p.lower() for kw in _INFO_KEYWORDS) or any(kw in p for kw in _INFO_KEYWORDS)
    ]
    # Need at least two intent-bearing fragments to justify decomposition.
    if len(informative) < 2:
        return [text]
    # Dedup while preserving order.
    seen, out = set(), []
    for p in informative:
        key = p.lower()
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        out.append(p)
        if len(out) >= max_parts:
            break
    return out or [text]

# --- REPLACE the existing single-shot RAG block in handle_knowledge ---
# OLD:
#     try:
#         knowledge_result = search_hotel_knowledge.invoke(last_user_message)
#         # Trim to prevent overshadowing the user question (max ~2000 chars)
#         if len(knowledge_result) > 2000:
#             knowledge_result = knowledge_result[:2000] + "\n..."
#     except Exception as e:
#         logger.error(f"RAG search failed: {e}")
#         knowledge_result = "No information found."

# NEW:
    try:
        sub_queries = _split_multi_intent(last_user_message)
        if len(sub_queries) > 1:
            logger.info(
                f"handle_knowledge: multi-intent decomposition -> {len(sub_queries)} sub-queries: "
                + " | ".join(q[:40] for q in sub_queries)
            )
            # Per-sub-query retrieval. We temporarily override num_docs via
            # env var so search_hotel_knowledge stays a pure tool with no
            # new signature. 3 chunks * up to 4 sub-queries = bounded context.
            prev_n = os.environ.get("HOTEL_RAG_NUM_DOCS")
            os.environ["HOTEL_RAG_NUM_DOCS"] = os.getenv("HOTEL_RAG_NUM_DOCS_PER_SUBQ", "3")
            try:
                blocks = []
                for i, sq in enumerate(sub_queries, 1):
                    try:
                        r = search_hotel_knowledge.invoke(sq)
                    except Exception as e:
                        logger.warning(f"handle_knowledge: sub-query {i} RAG failed: {e}")
                        r = "(no information found for this sub-question)"
                    # Per-sub-query trim so one fat block doesn't crowd out others.
                    if len(r) > 900:
                        r = r[:900] + "\n..."
                    blocks.append(f"[Q{i}: {sq}]\n{r}")
            finally:
                if prev_n is None:
                    os.environ.pop("HOTEL_RAG_NUM_DOCS", None)
                else:
                    os.environ["HOTEL_RAG_NUM_DOCS"] = prev_n
            knowledge_result = "\n\n===\n\n".join(blocks)
            # Final outer trim — keep total context bounded.
            if len(knowledge_result) > 2400:
                knowledge_result = knowledge_result[:2400] + "\n..."
        else:
            knowledge_result = search_hotel_knowledge.invoke(last_user_message)
            if len(knowledge_result) > 2000:
                knowledge_result = knowledge_result[:2000] + "\n..."
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"RAG search failed: {e}")
        knowledge_result = "No information found."
